newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes higher but remains vulnerable.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes higher but remains vulnerable.

text.p: Gold prices rebounded in a correction against a heavily oversold market that had fallen to three-year lows but a rally based on short-covering stopped on Wednesday before breaching resistance.
The market was energised by a 79-point fall in the Dow Jones Industrial Average in New York late on Tuesday and a weaker dollar which sent investers into gold after weeks of neglect.
Bullion fixed at $370.90 per ounce after $370.40 on Wednesday morning, which was three dollars above the lowest fixing since November 3, 1993 set on Tuesday afternoon.
New York prices were up as well.
At the fixing the February Comex contract was showing an intraday gain of $2.50 at $372.90
Even so, the base tone was still bearish. "Medium term we are still looking to the downside," a dealer said.
Investment fund buying was cited as spurring the overnight rally which brought in short covering from the professionals.

But dealers said producer selling was likely to continue to put pressure on prices as the miners protected their income. The impact of falling gold prices had been made the more adverse by movements in their local currencies against the dollar.
Persistent talk of a central bank gold sale within the past month or so also weighed on the market, dealers said.
Technically the gold market was still oversold, according to technical analysts, with a 14-day RSI of around 21 suggesting the support under $370.00 should hold.
But the downside risk remained. "Only if the $390.00 area could be cleared could the possibility of the fall extending to $350.00 be ignored," one technician said.
The other precious metals rallied behind gold although dealers said there was little interest being developed beyond the professionals.

Silver's resilience against a falling gold price could mean its low has been seen and "upside potential extends to levels just over $5.00," according to techncial analyst Elli Gifford at Investment Research of Cambridge.
Silver was indicated at $4.80/$4.82 at mid afternoon, a 10-cent gain from the Tuesday close.
Interest was very limited in platinum and palladium. Platinum was at $374.00/$375.00, $3.50 above the close and palladium was showing at $116.25/$117.25, a $2.00 gain.
